legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Memory Intelligence Agent" (MIA), Jingyang Qiao, Weicheng Meng et al. (ECNU, Shanghai Innovation Institute and others). Preprint, arXiv 2604.04503v4, 19 Apr 2026. No venue.

COVERAGE: Read the extraction of 117,818 chars (1,891 lines) in full: abstract, intro, method, experiments, ablations, conclusion, appendices A-G (prompts included). I skipped only the reference list (lines ~1183-1360) apart from a grep. A grep for token, cost, latency and storage found no cost measurement anywhere.

FIT WARNING: Partial fit. The paper is about memory for deep-research (search) agents, not chat or personal memory. It compares memory methods and has a raw-vs-distilled axis. It has NO token-matched comparison, NO full-context baseline, and NO cost, latency or storage numbers. The abstract and intro claim lower storage and retrieval cost, but the paper never measures them. Use it for "does memory help, and which form", not for "what does it cost".

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Raw-trajectory or long-context memory methods (RAG, Mem0, A-Mem) generally score below the no-memory baseline; distilled plan-style memory scores above it.
   number: text-only averages computed from Table 4: No Memory 41.2, RAG 39.2, Mem0 39.6, A-Mem 38.8, ReasoningBank 42.7. Multimodal FVQA-test: No Memory 61.4, RAG 60.5, Mem0 55.6, A-Mem 38.5, ReasoningBank 64.7. (The averages are my arithmetic, not the paper's.)
   setup: Qwen2.5-VL-7B Executor trained identically per variant, 7 multimodal and 4 text-only benchmarks, accuracy judged by Qwen3-32B.
   quote: "traditional contextual memory methods (e.g., RAG, Mem0, and A-Mem) generally underperform the "No Memory" baseline. This validates that long memory contexts introduce noise, leading to performance degradation."
   where: Sec 4.2, p13; Tables 3-4, p14-15.
2. MIA beats the best prior memory method by 5.5 points on multimodal average (53.6 average accuracy) and 7.5 on text-only (53.5).
   number: 5.5 / 7.5. Text-only per benchmark: MIA 47.7 / 71.8 / 63.5 / 31.1 vs No Memory 40.7 / 61.2 / 51.0 / 11.7 (SimpleQA / 2Wiki / HotpotQA / GAIA).
   setup: same as claim 1. The best prior method is Memento. TTL is 1 epoch, 4 rollouts per sample, run on the test stream itself.
   quote: "MIA improves the average accuracy by 5.5, including specific increases of 3.3 on FVQA-test, 6.4 on the multi-hop task LiveVQA, and an impressive 9.1 on the highly challenging custom task In-house 1."
   where: p13; text-only 7.5 on p13.
3. Ablation (the most useful result for raw vs distilled): feeding raw memory directly to the Executor hurts or does nothing, while feeding memory to a Planner that writes a plan helps.
   number: Only Memory -0.4 multimodal average vs Base; Memory for Planner +3.5 multimodal and +4.15 text-only. Table 6: Only Memory on SimpleQA 37.7 vs Base 40.7. Cumulative total over Base: +8.94 multimodal, +12.38 text-only.
   setup: Planner is Qwen3-32B for the early ablation rows, then a trained Qwen3-8B. Executor Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
   quote: "simply introducing non-parametric memory (Only Memory) leads to a performance drop in the average accuracy of multimodal tasks (-0.4). However, when we integrate memory specifically to guide the planning process (Memory for Planner), the performance significantly improves."
   where: Sec 4.6, p17; Tables 5-6.
4. Test-time learning (TTL), which updates the Planner's weights online as the test stream arrives, adds a lot on top of the memory store alone.
   number: Trained Planner to +TTL: LiveVQA 40.1 to 43.1, In-house 1 26.1 to 31.8. Average +3.23 multimodal, +2.64 text-only.
   setup: Planner updated by GRPO during inference, Executor frozen.
   quote: "Finally, we introduce the online TTL mechanism. This dynamic evolution process provides a substantial final push, further increasing the average accuracy by 3.23 (multimodal) and 2.64 (text-only)."
   where: p18.
5. Unsupervised mode (a reviewer plus area-chair LLM panel on Qwen3-32B replaces ground truth) gets close to supervised, and repeated passes keep improving. Unsupervised memory alone is unstable.
   number: epochs 59.6 to 61.1 to 61.7 (quoted); Table 7 unsupervised memory alone: LiveVQA 28.5 vs Base 33.0 and FVQA 57.6 vs 61.4. Text-only Table 4: unsupervised 46.6 / 71.6 / 61.7 / 30.1 vs supervised 47.7 / 71.8 / 63.5 / 31.1.
   quote: "relying solely on unsupervised non-parametric memory leads to unstable performance, whereas incorporating TTL on it yields substantial improvements."
   where: Sec 4.7, p18; Table 7, p19.
6. MIA also helps frontier closed-source Executors, but the gain shrinks as the base model gets stronger.
   number: GPT-5.4 +8.9 LiveVQA / +6.4 HotpotQA; Gemini-3-Flash +3.1 / +2.6; Claude-Sonnet-4.6 +1.8 / +1.7.
   setup: only the Planner is trained, against a ReAct baseline.
   quote: "GPT-5.4 benefits the most ( +8.9 on LiveVQA, +6.4 on HotpotQA), followed by Gemini-3-Flash ( +3.1 on LiveVQA, +2.6 on HotpotQA) and Claude-Sonnet-4.6 ( +1.8 on LiveVQA, +1.7 on HotpotQA)."
   where: Sec 4.4, p16 (Fig 8).

BASELINES: Direct Answer, Search Agent (ReAct, MMSearch-R1, plus numbers copied from DeepMMSearch-R1, WebWatcher and Deepeyes2 reports), and memory agents: No Memory, RAG, Mem0, A-Mem (raw "workflow memory prompt"), ReasoningBank, ExpeL, Memento (abstracted "plan prompt"), and MIA. All memory baselines share the same Executor training settings, with the extra prompt format as the only difference. There is no full-context baseline (no "put the whole history in the window" run). Tokens are NOT matched: no token counts for memory prompts, retrieval, TTL rollouts or Planner training are reported. MIA uses extra compute that the baselines do not: a Planner, a Qwen3-32B Manager and Judger, 4 rollouts per question, and a reflect-replan step. Memento's parametric retrieval was not used ("only their non-parametric version"). The No Memory row is the same as the "Base" row in the ablations. The Tool Call Analysis (Fig 9, p16-17) plots tool calls versus accuracy but reports no cost.

LIMITS: Conceded by the authors: "Currently, our framework primarily focuses on deep research tasks." Not shown in the paper:
- No storage, latency or token measurements, despite the cost framing.
- The Planner reward is noisy and slow to converge (Sec 4.3).
- The LiveVQA test set was swapped for a smaller public version (2,384 vs 3,602 items), so numbers are not comparable with MMSearch-R1.
- Two in-house benchmarks are not public. The judge is an LLM (Qwen3-32B), with no human check.
- Single runs, no variance or seeds reported.
- TTL trains on the test stream, so "out-of-domain" is soft.
- Several baseline numbers were copied from other papers.
- The generalization claim in the intro, "(4) MIA sets a new state-of-the-art", is relative to a weaker 7B setup.
- Closed-source Executor results are shown only as a chart (no table).

BUILDS ON (as printed): ReasoningBank (Ouyang et al., 2025); MemoryBank (Zhong et al., 2024); ExpeL (Zhao et al., 2024); Memento (Zhou et al., 2025); Mem0 (Chhikara et al., 2025); A-Mem (Xu et al., 2025); Mem-alpha (Wang et al., 2025a); Memory-R1 (Yan et al., 2025); MemEvolve (Zhang et al., 2025b); Evo-Memory (Wei et al., 2025); RAG (Lewis et al., 2020); Search-R1 (Jin et al., 2025); DeepResearcher (Zheng et al., 2025); MMSearch-R1 (Wu et al., 2025); DeepMMSearch-R1 (Narayan et al., 2025); GRPO (Shao et al., 2024); ReAct (Yao et al., 2023); veRL (Sheng et al., 2025); MATPO (Mo et al., 2025). It does not give venues in the body text.

CODE: Retrieval score, Appendix D, p25-26: Score(m_i) = λs*normSim_i + λv*Val_i + λf*Freq_i, with Val_i = s_i/(u_i+1), Freq_i = 1/(u_i+1), weights 0.7 / 0.3 / 0.3. Similarity is 0.8 question + 0.2 image caption. Planner reward, Eq. 4: 0.7*final-answer correct + 0.2*intermediate-answer correct + 0.05*reflection reward + 0.05*format.

FIGURES: Figure 3 (p5): "Reasoning process of MIA consists of three parts: Inputs & Retrieval... Research Process... Outputs & Storage", i.e. retrieve, plan and execute, then compress the trajectory into a workflow summary. It shows raw trajectory becoming distilled memory (caption plus abstract numbered workflow, with success counts) faster than prose can.

PROBLEMS: Equations and figure text are garbled in the extraction (Fig 1, Fig 8 and Fig 9 labels come out as noise). The numbers I quoted come from clean tables. I computed the averages in claim 1 myself. The PDF contains no instructions aimed at the reader; the prompts in Appendix G are task prompts for the system. The extracted text is at /tmp/mia/t.txt (scratch).
